crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Invoice Capture and Coding
children.blurb: Invoice capture and coding covers the intake of supplier invoices and the assignment of general ledger codes, cost centres and tax treatments before payment runs.

children.name: Customer Credit Risk
children.blurb: Customer credit risk is the chance that a buyer will not pay what they owe on the terms agreed, and it sits at the centre of receivables work.

children.name: Programmable Settlement and Escrow
children.blurb: Programmable settlement and escrow covers the use of software rules and smart contracts to hold funds and release them automatically when agreed conditions are met.

children.name: Collections and Payment Plans
children.blurb: Collections and payment plans cover the work of recovering money owed on overdue invoices and arranging structured schedules for customers who cannot pay in full on time.

children.name: Working Capital Timing
children.blurb: Working capital timing is the practice of managing when cash leaves and enters a business, chiefly through the gap between paying suppliers and collecting from customers.

sections.body: Payables and receivables is the money in and money out side of a business, and artificial intelligence is now doing much of the reading, matching and chasing that used to sit with clerks. Invoice capture systems read a PDF or a scan, pull out the vendor, amount, tax and line items, then code the charge to the right account and route it for approval. On the receivables side, models score how likely a customer is to pay late, decide which overdue accounts to chase first, and draft the reminder. Settlement itself is moving toward programmable rails, where payment releases when a condition is met rather than when a person clicks send. None of this removes the ledger or the bank, it just moves the judgement calls earlier and makes the routine ones automatic.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: Invoice capture is the most mature part and works well on clean, consistent documents, though odd layouts, poor scans and handwritten notes still need a person. Credit risk scoring is useful but inherits the bias and blind spots of the data it was trained on, and a model that has only seen a benign credit period can misjudge a downturn. Programmable settlement and escrow are real but narrow, mostly confined to specific chains and platforms, and the legal treatment of an automatic release is not settled everywhere. Collections automation raises its own questions about fairness and about what a machine is allowed to say to a debtor. Working capital timing is the least automated, because it depends on supplier relationships and negotiation as much as on forecasting. The honest limit across all of it is that these systems predict and prepare, they do not carry the liability when a payment is wrong.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The pages run roughly in the order money moves. Invoice Capture and Coding is the entry point, covering how a bill becomes a structured, approved entry, and it is the page to read first because everything downstream depends on clean data. Customer Credit Risk sits before the sale is agreed, explaining how a buyer's likelihood of paying is scored and where those scores fail. Programmable Settlement and Escrow covers the moment of payment, including conditional release and the platforms that support it. Collections and Payment Plans picks up after a due date passes, on prioritising outreach and structuring instalments. Working Capital Timing closes the loop, on how the gap between paying suppliers and being paid by customers is forecast and managed. Read together they describe one cycle, and each page is written to stand alone for a reader who only needs that stage.
